events.text: Analyst request: several cards this month show losses with no shared device. Review transaction 3660127 on card C06220-K1 and look for what the affected cards have in common.

events.msg: Core toolkit: flagged transaction, card window, card baseline, recurring charges, resolved account history, device neighbours, region activity and prior cases

hypotheses: The card is compromised as part of a coordinated fraud ring using spoofed device profiles (SM-J700T1 with inconsistent operating systems) across multiple unrelated accounts.
The transaction is a legitimate purchase by the cardholder, and the spoofed device signature is an anomalous false positive or shared generic profile.

calls.why: To identify all cards, transactions, and closed cases associated with the spoofed device profile 'SM-J700T1 |  |  | ' within the last 30 days.
To review the full transaction history of card C06220-K1 around the time of the flagged transaction to check for other suspicious activity.

events.msg: Four specialist analysts reviewing their evidence in parallel

events.assessment: The flagged transaction 3660127 is part of a highly suspicious daily sequence of high-value product C transactions (including 3660125 and 3660126) that deviate significantly from the card's historical baseline, where product C is extremely rare. These transactions all utilize anonymous proxies and present anomalous device signatures, such as an Android hardware identifier (SM-J700T1) paired with iOS operating systems.
key_points: A distinct daily velocity pattern is observed with transactions 3660125, 3660126, and 3660127 occurring approximately 24 hours apart for amounts of $637.13, $758.80, and $770.78 respectively.
The card's baseline shows product C was only purchased twice out of 366 historical transactions, making this sudden burst highly anomalous.
All three high-value transactions utilized anonymous proxies (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS) and spoofed device profiles, combining an Android model string (SM-J700T1) with iOS user agents.

events.assessment: The card C06220-K1 shows a shift from its initial transaction 3627503, which used a Windows 7 desktop device, to a new mobile device profile. This flagged mobile device (SM-J700T1) is not only new to the card but also connected via an anonymous proxy, indicating a high likelihood of unauthorized card-not-present activity.
key_points: Card C06220-K1 was first observed in transaction 3627503 using a Windows 7 desktop device with a low transaction model risk of 0.006964.
The flagged device profile (SM-J700T1) is marked as New and has zero previous associations with this card.
The connection for the flagged device utilized an anonymous proxy (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS), which is a strong indicator of fraud.

events.assessment: The investigation of transaction 3660127 on card C06220-K1 reveals no connections to other cards, devices, or cases within the provided network data. Although the transaction utilized an anonymous proxy, both the bank's real-time risk score and the transaction model probability indicate very low risk.
key_points: Transaction 3660127 on card C06220-K1 shows a low real-time risk score of 0.07 and a transaction model probability of 0.012414.
The device associated with transaction 3660127 is linked to only one card (C06220-K1) and one customer (C06220) across all time.
The transaction was conducted via an anonymous proxy (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS), which is a notable technical detail but unsupported by other risk indicators.

events.assessment: The analyst request asks to review transaction 3660127 on card C06220-K1 and identify commonalities among affected cards. Historical cases for card C06220-K1 show a recurring pattern of confirmed fraud across multiple months, alternating between card-not-present fraud and out-of-region card-present use, despite repeated card blocks and reissues.
key_points: Card C06220-K1 has been associated with five confirmed fraud cases (CC-0626, CC-2539, CC-2807, CC-4224, and CC-5379) between July and October 2016.

The fraud patterns alternate between card-not-present fraud (CC-0626, CC-4224) using generic mobile devices and out-of-region card-present fraud (CC-2539, CC-2807, CC-5379) while the cardholder retained possession of the physical card.
One case (CC-0815) was cleared as non-fraudulent after the cardholder confirmed a transaction from a new phone.

events.claim: The transaction model, trained on the bank's own closed cases from July to October (its July-September version scored AUC 0.972 on October), scores this transaction 0.012, against a 2.0% base rate. It reads the unnamed Vesta C/D/M/V columns, the identity record, running aggregates of the resolved account and the graph's memory of earlier closed cases, all as known at transaction time. January activity is newer than anything the model learned from and carries patterns it has never seen, so a low score counts at most as weak evidence of innocence: its weight is bounded to between 0.5 and 8
The purchase came from a device profile marked New for this account and never seen on this card before (SM-J700T1 |  |  | )
The session was routed through an anonymous proxy

This card has 1 earlier alert(s) that were cleared as false alarms (CC-0815; latest note: "Case CC-0815: model scored a $74.91 transaction at 0.92. Cardholder confirmed the purchase from a new phone. Device added to profile. Alert cleared.")

3 online purchase(s) ($637.13, $758.80, $770.78) from a device that reports itself as 'SM-J700T1', an Android handset, but with operating system(s) (blank), iOS 11.1.1, iOS 11.1.2: a fingerprint no real device produces, marked New for this account, 3 behind an anonymising proxy

The same spoofed device fingerprint signature appears on 4 other card(s) in the same 30 days (C05061-K1, C05704-K2, C07925-K1, C11309-K1): coordinated activity across customers, not one cardholder's habit

events.claim: Containment plan for the analyst (this case's own actions cover only its card): the 5-card ring has $7,610.94 at risk. Every ring card clears the 0.7 confidence bar on its own evidence, so the plan blocks all 5 (C06220-K1, C05061-K1, C11309-K1, C07925-K1, C05704-K2), cutting 100% of it; an expected 0.7 of them could still belong to customers who are not compromised. Blocked at under 0.9 confidence, named for review: C05061-K1, C11309-K1, C07925-K1, C05704-K2.
